name: Seymour Brunson
role: Early elder and member of the Nauvoo high council
dateNote: He was baptized in January 1831, called to preach by section 75 in 1832, and died at Nauvoo on 10 August 1840.
importance: Section 75 pairs him with Daniel Stanton for preaching in 1832. He later moved to Missouri and joined the Nauvoo high council in 1839. At his funeral on 15 August 1840, Joseph Smith first taught publicly that the living could be baptized for the dead. Section 124 lists him on the high council with the note “I have taken unto myself”.
connections: Baptized by Solomon Hancock. Section 124 names Aaron Johnson to take his place on the high council.

sources.title: Baptism for the Dead, Church History Topics
